rich_narrative.summary: The Center for Islamic Teachings and Community Development provides <cite id="5">religious education, cemetery services, and community programs</cite> for the Muslim community in North America. Founded in <cite id="5">2012</cite>, the organization operates key institutions including the <cite id="5">Abraar Academy and the American Muslim Cemetery</cite>. In FY2024, the charity managed <cite id="3">$1,955,187 in total revenue</cite> to support its core religious and local infrastructure services. Financial filings indicate a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 100.0% in FY2024</cite>, which exceeds the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 96.9%</cite>. The organization is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite> and directs funds toward valid categories including <cite id="2">fuqara, masakin, and fisabilillah</cite>. However, evaluation shows significant reserves equal to <cite id="1">126.5 months of working capital</cite>, which creates a potential delay in deploying collected donor funds. Additionally, public outcome data remains limited across its educational and funeral service initiatives.
